output.root_problem: Shipment notices sent by ORG-A to ORG-B (handoff H-1, process P-1) are being rejected by ORG-B's carrier validation checks because the notice content/format mismatches ORG-B's business validation rules — manifested as distinct categorized reject reasons (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) rather than one generic data-entry-mistake class — not because of random correctable field errors or carrier-system flakiness (E-01; H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH, SUPPORTED).
output.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them to the carrier (SH-REQ's initial request, CL-01/CL-02), premised on rejects being flaky-carrier or data-entry issues fixable by resubmission.
symptoms: Reject-log shows 3 shipment notices rejected by ORG-B's carrier system: 2 categorized as LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and 1 as EVENT_ORDER (N-3) (E-01, F-01).
output.affected_process: P-1 shipment notice process (ORG-A to ORG-B)
causal_chain: ORG-A (Shipper) sends shipment notices to ORG-B (Carrier) via handoff H-1 within process P-1.
ORG-B's carrier system applies business validation rules to incoming notices and rejects those that fail validation, recorded in the reject log DA-REJ.
The reject log categorizes rejects into distinct reasons - 2x LOC_UNKNOWN, 1x EVENT_ORDER - rather than one generic data-entry-mistake class (E-01).

This categorization pattern supports a mismatch between ORG-B's validation rules and ORG-A's notice content/format (H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH), as opposed to random correctable data-entry slips or transient carrier flakiness.
Resulting symptom: shipment notices submitted by ORG-A are rejected by ORG-B, requiring manual handling instead of flowing through automatically.

assumptions.statement: The 3-record reject-log sample used to categorize reject reasons is representative of the broader, ongoing pattern of carrier rejects rather than an atypical snapshot.
The LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reject codes indicate structural validation-rule mismatches rather than isolated correctable field typos or transient timing/system issues.
DA-REJ (carrier reject log) accurately and sufficiently reflects all rejects relevant to P-1 despite its completeness being marked UNKNOWN.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): ORG-A's shipment notices (handoff H-1) are rejected by ORG-B's carrier validation checks because notice content/format mismatches ORG-B's business rules, evidenced by distinct reject-reason categories rather than one generic data-entry class (E-01, F-01).

The initial request (CL-01, CL-02) was to deploy an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejected notices on the premise that rejects are flaky-carrier or data-entry issues. This premise (hypothesis H-AUTOFIX-FIXABLE-ERRORS) was tested and REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02; H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH is instead SUPPORTED by E-01, while H-CARRIER-FLAKY remains only a CANDIDATE resting on the stakeholder's own unverified opinion (E-02).

Problem establishment went through the DEFINE gate, which returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical unknowns (U-SAMPLE-ADEQUACY, U-REASON-ROOT-CAUSE-TYPE) to verification obligations VOB-U-SAMPLE-ADEQUACY and VOB-U-REASON-ROOT-CAUSE-TYPE rather than resolving them.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no items on hold. Only one scope item is actually released: consult_interface_owner:SH-INT (per solution_design.release_scope); analyze_reject_reasons:DA-REJ and compare_notice_content_to_carrier_rules:H-1 are not released this cycle.

Reason the release proceeded as scoped: VOB-U-SAMPLE-ADEQUACY and VOB-U-REASON-ROOT-CAUSE-TYPE remain OPEN but their blocking_scope (analyze_reject_reasons:DA-REJ, compare_notice_content_to_carrier_rules:H-1) falls outside the released scope, so they did not block the SH-INT consult item. A third obligation, VOB-R-3 (about whether a return handoff from ORG-B to ORG-A conveying reject reasons exists, i.e. H-FEEDBACK-GAP), does intersect the released scope but is flagged non-critical (impact MEDIUM) and open.

A pending plan item (W-WI-CONSULT-SH-INT) notes that no catalog operation currently exists to actually execute consult_interface_owner:SH-INT, and that VOB-R-3 blocks this exact scope item, so the released scope item is not yet operationally executable this cycle.
limitations_explained: The dominant reject-reason pattern (2 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1 EVENT_ORDER) rests on only 3 reject records (E-01) and is explicitly flagged inadequate by VOB-U-SAMPLE-ADEQUACY (HIGH impact), so it is not yet statistically established; this inadequacy is not addressed by this release.

Whether LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER reflect correctable field errors, systemic rule mismatches, or timing/sequencing issues remains undetermined (VOB-U-REASON-ROOT-CAUSE-TYPE, CRITICAL impact, OPEN), and the related assumption A-CODES-REFLECT-RULE-MISMATCH is only an active assumption, not a confirmed fact.

Because analyze_reject_reasons:DA-REJ and compare_notice_content_to_carrier_rules:H-1 remain blocked by these open critical verification obligations, root-cause mapping (success criterion SC-ROOT-CAUSE-MAPPED) cannot complete this cycle; only the SH-INT consultation item is released.

Whether a feedback handoff exists from ORG-B back to ORG-A carrying reject-reason codes (H-FEEDBACK-GAP) is unresolved (VOB-R-3, open, non-critical but intersecting released scope), so it is unknown whether the same reject types will keep recurring due to a visibility gap.

The data asset underlying the analysis, DA-REJ (carrier reject log), has UNKNOWN completeness, and the assumption that it sufficiently reflects all relevant rejects (A-REJECT-LOG-SCOPE) and that the 3-record sample generalizes (A-SAMPLE-GENERALIZES) are both unverified assumptions, not confirmed facts.
output.summary: The problem, as formally defined in PD-1, is that ORG-A's shipment notices (handoff H-1) are being rejected by ORG-B's carrier validation checks because the notice content/format mismatches ORG-B's business rules — observed as distinct categorized reject reasons (2 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1 EVENT_ORDER) rather than one generic class of data-entry mistakes (E-01, F-01). This was established by testing the stakeholder's original request (CL-01/CL-02: deploy an AI agent to auto-fix and blindly resubmit rejected notices, premised on carrier flakiness or correctable typos) as a hypothesis (H-AUTOFIX-FIXABLE-ERRORS), which was REJECTED by the evidence, while H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH is SUPPORTED by E-01; the alternative flaky-carrier narrative (H-CARRIER-FLAKY) rests only on the unverified stakeholder claim E-02. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical unknowns to open verification obligations rather than resolving them. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with nothing held: only the consult_interface_owner:SH-INT scope item is actually released (per SD-1's release_scope), while the deeper reject-reason analysis and content-vs-rules comparison remain blocked. This narrow release was possible because the two most critical open obligations (sample adequacy, root-cause type) block scope items outside what was released, though a third, non-critical obligation (VOB-R-3, about a possible feedback-handoff gap) does intersect the released scope and remains open. A pending plan item further notes no catalog operation yet exists to actually execute the released consult_interface_owner:SH-INT action. Known limitations: the 2:1 reject-reason pattern is based on only 3 records and is flagged as an inadequate sample; whether those reasons are rule mismatches, data errors, or timing issues is undetermined; root-cause mapping cannot complete this cycle; and it is unknown whether ORG-B ever reports reject reasons back to ORG-A.
